entities.summary:
Bernard Jarre, a French Cardinal, played a crucial role in the Avignon papacy (1309-1377).

Born during the Carolingian Renaissance, Jarre's early life and education were shaped by the tumultuous 13th-century Europe.

Jarre's appointment as Cardinal by Pope Urban V in 1362 marked a pivotal moment in his life, as he became a key figure in the papal court. His involvement in the Avignon papacy led to significant diplomatic efforts, particularly with the Kingdom of France.

Jarre's legacy extends to his influence on the development of medieval cardinals and their role in shaping the Catholic Church's governance. His position as a mediator between the papacy and European monarchies highlights the complexities of power dynamics in the 14th century.

The Avignon papacy, marked by the Babylonian captivity of the papacy, left an indelible mark on Western Christendom. Bernard Jarre's participation in this era underscores the intricate web of alliances and rivalries between the Church and European nations.

Despite the ephemeral nature of the Avignon papacy, Bernard Jarre's contributions to the Church's politics and the medieval European landscape remain noteworthy.
